    Trim-and-fill adjustment for funnel plot asymmetry

    Source: R/meta-bias.R
    meta_trimfill.Rd

    meta_trimfill() implements the non-parametric trim-and-fill method of Duval and Tweedie (2000). Studies on the more extreme side of the funnel are iteratively trimmed until the remaining studies are symmetric; the trimmed studies are then mirrored around the adjusted centre to impute the studies that appear to be missing, and the meta-analysis is refitted. The side of the funnel with missing studies is estimated from the sign of Egger's slope unless side is given.

    Usage

    meta_trimfill(
  .data,
  yi = .yi,
  vi = .vi,
  side = NULL,
  estimator = c("L0", "R0"),
  method = "REML",
  level = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame, <meta_es> or <meta_fit> from meta_pool().

    yi, vi

    <data-masking> Columns holding the effect sizes and sampling variances. Default to .yi and .vi.

    side

    "left" or "right", the side with missing studies. Estimated when NULL.

    estimator

    "L0" or "R0" estimator of the number of missing studies.

    method

    Estimator of \(\tau^2\), taken from the fit when .data is a <meta_fit>.

    level

    Confidence level for intervals.

    Value

    A <meta_fit> fitted to the observed and filled studies. glance() reports the number of filled studies (k0) and the side, and augment() flags the filled studies.

    Details

    Trim-and-fill is a sensitivity analysis: the filled studies are not real and the adjusted estimate should be interpreted with caution.

    References

    Duval, S. and Tweedie, R. (2000). Trim and fill: a simple funnel-plot-based method of testing and adjusting for publication bias in meta-analysis. Biometrics, 56(2), 455-463. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341x.2000.00455.x

    Examples

    bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg
)
meta_pool(bcg) |> meta_trimfill()
#> # Trim-and-fill adjusted meta-analysis <meta_fit>
#> # Model: random effects, restricted maximum likelihood
#> # Measure: log risk ratio; k = 14
#> # tau^2 = 0.3313; I^2 = 92.14%; H^2 = 12.72
#> # Q(13) = 154.68, p < 0.0001
#> # Studies filled on the right side: 1
#> # 95% prediction interval: [-1.8382, 0.5240]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   term    estimate std.error statistic  p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 overall   -0.657     0.179     -3.68 0.000233    -1.01    -0.307
